newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: C&P Homes rises 6.25 percent in Manila.
newsitem.headline: C&P Homes rises 6.25 percent in Manila.

text.p: Mass housing builder C&P Homes gained 75 centavos, or 6.25 percent, to 12.75 pesos in late trade on foreign buying, brokers said on Monday.
"Three foreign brokerage firms are buying into the issue in behalf of their clients ahead of 1997," one broker who asked not be named said.
Henry Ong at Sapphire Securities said C&P was selling because investors believe it's involvement in the mass housing sector has lower risk compared to upscale condominium and office developments.
Foreign investors sold down real estate issues last month on fears the Philippine property boom maybe fizzling out.
"But C&P's exposure is a different play because demand for low-cost housing units in the country is still tremendous," said Ong.
Ong said C&P was trading at 15 times its projected 1997 PE as against 20 times for other Philippine property issues.
